text: For the choir director: to the tune "Do Not Destroy." A miktam of David, when Saul sent men to watch his house in order to kill him.
Rescue me from my enemies, my God; set me safe above those who rise against me.
Rescue me from those who do evil; save me from bloodthirsty men.

versions.text: Rescue me from those who do evil; save me from men of blood.
versions.explanation: "Men of blood" is a literal Hebraism that may puzzle listeners; "bloodthirsty men" conveys the same sense clearly and flows better in oral reading.

text: See how they lie in wait for my life! Fierce men band together against me, though I have done no wrong, committed no sin, O LORD.
For no guilt of mine they run and take their positions. Rise up to meet me, and see!
You, LORD God of hosts, God of Israel, awake to punish all the nations; show no mercy to those who treacherously do evil. Selah
They return at evening, snarling like dogs, prowling around the city.
See how they pour out words with their mouths; swords are on their lips—"For who is listening?" they say.

versions.text: See how they spew from their mouths; swords are on their lips. "For who is listening?" they say.
versions.explanation: "Spew from their mouths" leaves the verb without an object and sounds abrupt when read aloud; the Hebrew יַבִּיעוּן pictures gushing speech. Supplying "words" clarifies the image and improves the oral flow, and the dash ties the quoted taunt to the line.

text: But you, LORD, laugh at them; you mock all the nations.
O my Strength, I keep watch for you, for God is my fortress.

versions.text: My strength, I watch for you, for God is my fortress.
versions.explanation: The line is a direct address to God; without the vocative "O" the phrase can be misheard as a statement about the speaker's own strength. Capitalizing "Strength" as a divine title and using "keep watch" matches the refrain in verse 18 and reads more naturally aloud.

text: My God of mercy will come to meet me; God will let me look in triumph on my foes.
Do not kill them, or my people will forget. Make them stagger by your power and bring them down, O Lord, our shield.
For the sin of their mouths, for the words of their lips, let them be caught in their own pride, for the curses and the lies they tell.
Consume them in wrath, consume them till they are no more; then they will know that God rules over Jacob to the ends of the earth. Selah
They return at evening, snarling like dogs, prowling around the city.
They roam about for food, and if they are not filled, they howl through the night.
But I will sing of your strength; in the morning I will sing aloud of your mercy, for you have been my fortress, my refuge in the day of my distress.
O my Strength, to you I sing praise, for God is my fortress, my God of mercy.

versions.text: My strength, to you I sing praise, for God is my fortress, my God of mercy.
versions.explanation: As in verse 10, the opening is a vocative addressed to God. Adding "O" and capitalizing the divine title makes the address unmistakable when the psalm is read aloud.
